signals.name: Going concern
signals.description: Going concern language indicating substantial doubt about ability to continue
phrases: ability to continue as a going concern

signals.name: Liquidity / covenant breach
signals.description: Liquidity shortfall or covenant breach

signals.name: Debt maturity / refinancing risk
signals.description: Debt maturity wall or refinancing risk

signals.name: Auditor emphasis of matter
signals.description: Auditor emphasis of matter or going concern paragraph
phrases: material uncertainty related to going concern

signals.name: Covenant / waiver risk
signals.description: Covenant or waiver language (legacy)

signals.name: Potential default
signals.description: Default or acceleration language

signals.name: Dropdown / guarantee release
signals.description: Transfer of assets from guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted subs or release of guarantees; value can be pledged to new debt without sharing with existing lenders (J.Crew-style).

signals.name: S-Prime / collateral leakage
signals.description: Priming of junior secured debt ahead of existing liens or covenant/structural features that allow value to leave the secured group; dilutes first-lien recovery.

signals.name: Uptiering
signals.description: Participating lenders consent to new debt ranking above existing debt (superpriority, roll-up); non-participating lenders left junior without consent.

signals.name: Texas two-step / structural merger
signals.description: Divisional or divisive merger separating liabilities from operating assets (e.g. mass tort in one entity); can reshape which assets back which creditors.

signals.name: Double-dip / triple-dip
signals.description: Structure creating multiple claims on same economic exposure (non-guarantor/empty-box sub, intercompany loan, parent guarantee); dilutes recovery for existing lenders.

signals.name: Consent solicitation / exchange / tender
signals.description: Out-of-court LME: consent solicitation (amendments for consent payment), exchange offer, tender offer, amend-and-extend; can change priority without bankruptcy.

signals.name: Equity cure
signals.description: Right for borrower or sponsor to inject equity to cure a covenant breach and avoid default; often limited by frequency and dollar cap.

signals.name: Substantive consolidation / cramdown
signals.description: Substantive consolidation (merging entities' assets/liabilities in bankruptcy); cramdown (plan confirmed over objection); absolute priority and fair and equitable.

signals.name: Lender voting squeeze
signals.description: Document mechanics allowing majority/required lenders to amend without consent of non-consenting or out-of-the-money lenders (yank-a-bank, snooze-you-lose).

signals.name: Forbearance / standstill
signals.description: Lenders agree not to exercise remedies (forbearance) or to refrain from enforcing (standstill) for a period; indicates default or workout mode.

signals.name: Crossover / bridge / prepack
signals.description: Financing intended to cross into Ch. 11 (crossover/bridge); prepack or pre-arranged bankruptcy; plan support agreement. Indicates contemplated or agreed bankruptcy path.

signals.name: Make-whole / disallowance
signals.description: Make-whole premium on early redemption/acceleration; in bankruptcy, claim disallowance (§ 502(b)) and unmatured interest can reduce allowed claim and recovery.

signals.name: Payment-in-kind (PIK)
signals.description: Interest paid in kind (added to principal) or PIK toggle (borrower elects PIK instead of cash); common in stressed structures; election signals covenant or liquidity pressure.

signals.name: J.Crew blocker / anti-dropdown
signals.description: Covenant provision restricting transfer of IP or key assets to unrestricted subsidiaries (J.Crew 2017: $250M IP dropdown); presence protects lenders, absence is critical vulnerability.
phrases: ip cannot be transferred to unrestricted

signals.name: Serta / Rite Aid uptier
signals.description: Non-consensual uptier where majority lenders (>50%) issue super-priority debt, subordinating minority without consent (Serta 2020, Rite Aid 2020); lender-on-lender violence.

signals.name: Incora / Wesco vote rigging
signals.description: Strategic debt issuance to affiliates to manipulate voting thresholds and achieve synthetic majority (Incora/Wesco 2020); forces non-participating lenders into amendments.
phrases: debt issued to affiliate to manipulate vote
